findings.claim: Guru Granth Sahib page 94 affirms that God created the universe and placed his light (Jot) within all created beings
findings.truth: Ang 94 is Maajh, Fourth Mehl: it opens with the Mool Mantar (God as Karta Purakh) and is a devotional composition on longing for the Guru and the Naam. It carries no creation-and-Jot teaching. The 'light within all' teaching is ang 349, which the spec names at 1.6.
findings.evidence: srigranth.org ang 94 full line list; spec 2G 1.2 names GGS 12 and 94 for God as Creator

findings.claim: Guru Granth Sahib page 12 states that the Creator has created the world through his word (Shabad)
findings.truth: Ang 12 reads 'You created the creation; You behold it and understand it' and 'This human body has been given to you. This is your chance to meet the Lord of the Universe.' It has no Shabad-creation line.

findings.claim: Guru Granth Sahib page 2 teaches that those who serve the Guru receive liberation
findings.truth: Ang 2 (Japji, pauri 4) reads 'By the karma of past actions, the robe of this physical body is obtained. By His Grace, the Gate of Liberation is found.' The page makes grace, not service to the Guru, the route to liberation - which is also the point the lesson argues two sentences later.

findings.claim: 12 marks - Discuss a Statement / 'Discuss this statement.' in all four lessons, and 'the 12-mark Discuss question' in three exam tips
findings.truth: Discuss is not a command word for this qualification. The spec's command-word appendix lists State, Outline, Describe, Explain and Evaluate; the 12-mark AO2 question is Evaluate.

findings.claim: '3 marks - Describe' question in every lesson
findings.truth: Paper 2 sets two questions, each (a) Outline three - 3 marks, (b) Explain two - 4, (c) Explain two with a source of wisdom and authority - 5, (d) Evaluate - 12 (48 + 3 SPaG = 51). Describe is a 4-mark command word in the spec's appendix, so a 3-mark Describe is an impossible tariff. Converted to the paper's 3-mark Outline three form; the three-point mark schemes already fit.
findings.evidence: spec Paper 2 overview (lines 338-390), assessment information (line 2727), command-word table (lines 4275-4360)

findings.claim: Guru Granth Sahib page 349 states: “Recognise the divine light within all, and do not discriminate on the basis of birth.”
findings.truth: Words inside quotation marks that are not the text. Ang 349 (Asa, First Mehl) reads 'Recognise the Lord's light within all, and do not consider social class or status; there are no classes or castes in the world hereafter.'

findings.claim: Guru Granth Sahib page 125 describes haumai as the great disease (repeated in the Key Fact and quoted in knowledge check 1)
findings.truth: 'Ego is a chronic disease, but it contains its own cure as well' is ang 466, not ang 125. Ang 125 says 'The Gurmukhs have the pain of egotism taken away.' The spec still names 125, so the source reference stands; only the wording was wrong.

findings.claim: Guru Granth Sahib page 226 teaches that through the Guru's grace, haumai is overcome
findings.truth: Ang 226 reads 'Egotism is overcome only by contemplating the Word of the Guru's Shabad.' Naming the Shabad is the better exam answer.

findings.claim: The Guru Granth Sahib is present inside [the Harmandir Sahib] day and night, and scripture is read continuously
findings.truth: The Guru Granth Sahib is seated in the Harmandir Sahib for about 20 hours a day; each night it is carried in a palki to its bedroom in the Akal Takht (sukhasan) and returned at dawn (prakash).

findings.claim: The Nitnem consists of five set prayers ... These prayers come from the Guru Granth Sahib
findings.truth: Jaap Sahib and Tav-Prasad Savaiye are compositions of Guru Gobind Singh in the Dasam Granth, not the Guru Granth Sahib. Only Japji Sahib, Rahiras and Kirtan Sohila are Guru Granth Sahib banis.

findings.claim: Guru Granth Sahib page 305 teaches the importance of prayer both in the morning and at night (repeated as a model source in practice question 4)
findings.truth: Ang 305 is the amrit vela teaching: 'One who calls himself a Sikh of the Guru, the True Guru, shall rise in the early morning hours and meditate on the Lord's Name', then remember God through the day. It sets no night prayer.

findings.claim: Nishan Sahib: the orange or dark-blue triangular flag
findings.truth: The Nishan Sahib is saffron in almost every gurdwara; dark blue is the Nihang variant. Leading with 'orange or dark-blue' as equal options is loose but not false, so no edit.

findings.claim: Guru Granth Sahib page 1391 affirms that the gurdwara belongs to all - it is the Guru's house, open to everyone
findings.truth: Ang 1391 is a Bhatt savaiya in praise of Guru Angad: 'Through the Guru's Door, the Gurdwara, You have conquered the world; You play the game even-handedly.' The gloss over-reads, but 'even-handedly' keeps it defensible and the spec names 1391 for the gurdwara. No edit.

findings.claim: The martyrdom of Guru Arjan ... is also commemorated during the Divali/Bandi Chhor Divas period / is also remembered in this period
findings.truth: Guru Arjan died on 30 May 1606. His Shaheedi Divas falls in May or June, months away from Divali. Only Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom day (November) sits near it, and that is a separate day too.

findings.claim: Rahit Maryada Chapters 11-13 govern Amrit Sanskar (in the content, Key Fact, conclusion, exam tip, mark scheme and glossary)
findings.truth: The spec names Rahit Maryada Chapters 11 and 13. Written as a range it wrongly claims Chapter 12 as well.

findings.claim: Amrit Sanskar ... initiates Khalsa Sikhs who receive the Five Ks
findings.truth: A candidate must already be wearing the Five Ks when they present themselves for amrit; they are not given at the ceremony.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Amrit Sanchar (Sikh Rehat Maryada requirement)

findings.claim: readers must be initiated Khalsa Sikhs (stated as a Rahit Maryada Chapter 7 rule for the akhand path, and repeated as an acceptable answer in practice question 1)
findings.truth: I could not verify an amritdhari-only rule for akhand path readers. The Rehat Maryada chapter is about unbroken reading by a team who can read Gurbani accurately, and the family are encouraged to take part; SGPC and searchgurbani both refused the fetch. Options: (a) soften to 'the readers must be Sikhs who can read Gurbani accurately, and the family often take a turn', which is safe either way; (b) leave and verify against the Rehat Maryada text. Recommend (a).
findings.evidence: sgpc.net 403, searchgurbani 403, Wikipedia Akhand Path silent on reader status
findings.ruling: Leave: unverifiable claim (sources 403 / no article); not mark-affecting.

findings.claim: Sikh Divali is never named Bandi Chhor Divas in the body text
findings.truth: Bandi Chhor Divas is the Sikh name for the day. The F14 edit removed the only mention (inside a definition), so the name is restored in the sentence about lighting lamps.

findings.claim: 'SPaG rewards correct spelling of ...' at the end of all four exam tips
findings.truth: SPaG is 3 of the 51 marks and is assessed on one Evaluate question, not across the paper. The tips do not say this, but a student could read them as SPaG credit everywhere. Not worth an edit on its own; worth folding into any later exam-tip pass.
findings.evidence: spec Paper 2 overview (5% SPaG) and assessment information

summary: Every lesson had errors. Four are HIGH: an invented Guru Granth Sahib 94 teaching taught in six places, a misquoted ang 349, two Nitnem prayers wrongly said to come from the Guru Granth Sahib, and Guru Arjan's martyrdom placed at Divali. The exam frame was also wrong: 'Discuss' for the 12-mark question (this board uses Evaluate) and a 3-mark 'Describe' question that this paper never sets.
